layer: it could not be reviewed, versioned or provisioned per project. It also could not
run at all — topology-router was never one of the declared seams, so its model never
resolved and the LLM path threw at module load. Every topology decision in every run has
NO PROJECT FACT APPEARS HERE. The stories, the phase and the CPA signals arrive as values.
What stays is the decision rule, which is a fact about orchestration, not about a codebase.
description: Choose the execution topology for a phase, given each story's effort, role, dependencies and cost signals.
body:
You are selecting an execution topology for orchestration phase "__PHASE__".

Stories to classify:
__STORIES__
__CPA_SIGNALS__

Rules:
- single: 0-1 worktree stories, OR one high-effort story that needs focused attention
- parallel: 2-4 independent stories with no shared file scope
- sequential: stories with overlapping file scope, tight coupling, or shared state risk

Overlapping file scope outranks story count. Stories that edit the same file must not run in
parallel worktrees, even when there are only two or three of them: the count alone cannot see
that, and parallel worktrees over a shared file produce a merge conflict the run cannot resolve.

Respond with ONLY this JSON object. No prose, no markdown fences:
{"topology":"single|parallel|sequential","reason":"<one sentence naming the deciding factor>"}
$mayBeEmptyWhy: A phase can genuinely have no cost signals — CPA runs per story and a phase may hold none yet. Absent is a REAL state here, not a failed lookup, so the section renders blank rather than the render refusing. Every other placeholder must be supplied: an empty story list or phase name would mean the caller asked about nothing.
